Subject: BlueMesh / Redwood - post-call ops synthesis and next steps

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the candid discussion on where BlueMesh is trying to get to. Quick recap from my side and proposed short-term next steps so we keep momentum.

Key pain points you articulated
- Search latency spikes during peak (10–11am PT) causing user drop-off — important to keep interactive queries <120ms p95 for short prompts.
- Cost is material for the personalization pipeline (millions of requests/day) — want predictable unit economics.
- PHI and contractual controls: need VPC-only private deployment, strict KMS, and audit logging for compliance.

Goals we aligned on
1) Pilot: run real-time semantic search (average prompt ~40 tokens) with p95 latency target <= 120ms and p99 <= 500ms under 600 qps steady-state (bursts to 1.5k qps).
2) Batch: nightly summarization for long documents (~2k tokens) with throughput target ~100 concurrent jobs and an acceptable latency window of 5–10 minutes/job.
3) Security: Private deployment (VPC), KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence mirroring your controls.

Immediate next steps (owners + timing)
- Technical topology & sizing proposal from Redwood (Irene) — deliver by end of day Thurs (02/19).
- Provide sample traces & a 1000-row prompt set (BlueMesh) so we can run microbenchmarks (Amit).
- Lock a 90-minute SRE workshop to walk the pilot runbook and mutual action plan (Jordan / Marissa) — propose week of 02/23.

Attachments: Irenes's topology diagram and a draft mutual-action-plan will follow.

If anything above doesn't match your notes, flag it and I'll correct. Otherwise I'll treat these as our working assumptions for the proposal.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Jordan — copying what I'll send as the short technical proposal so we have it on record. I've included rough capacity math and deployment options; we can tighten estimates once we run your sample traces.

Quoted from Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai> on Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 4:12 PM:> Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the candid discussion on where BlueMesh is trying to get to....

High-level topology (recommended for pilot)
- Private Control Plane (Redwood Private) with customer VPC peering; data plane hosts in dedicated subnet. KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping. Audit logs streamed to your logging endpoint.
- Dual pool strategy:
  * Real-time pool (interactive search): 8 x H100-equivalent GPUs in dedicated cluster. Model: open-architecture 13B -> 70B family (we recommend 13B or 33B quantized for tight latency). Autoscale floor: 4 GPUs; ceiling: 12 GPUs with burst routing.
  * Batch pool (summarization): 4 x A100-style GPUs optimized for long-context runs (up to 4k tokens) — prefer larger memory instances to avoid KV overflow.

Throughput & latency estimates (ballpark; run on your traces to validate)
- Interactive search (13B quantized int8, sequence 40 tokens request / 128 max): ~150–220 qps per H100 GPU sustained with smart batching and KV prefix caching. With 8 GPUs steady state -> ~1.2k–1.7k qps. Expected p95 latency ~70–160ms depending on batching policy; we configure SLO window to keep p95 <= 120ms via adaptive batching and small-batch prioritization.
- Quantization: we recommend int8 with per-channel calibration for the pilot. If quality/regression tests pass, we can move to 4-bit quant (LLM Q4_0) for extra cost savings in the next phase.
- Batch summarization: a single A100-equivalent supports ~6–8 concurrent long-context jobs (2k tokens) with average runtime ~90–180s; scale horizontally to meet the 100 concurrent job target.

Availability & fallbacks
- Multi-tier routing: primary -> dedicated pool; fallback -> smaller quantized model in a hosted cold pool to absorb burst traffic when dedicated capacity hits ceiling.
- Canary config for rollouts and automatic fallback on latency violations.

Security & compliance notes
- Private-only deployment with VPC peering and per-route egress controls.
- We’ll provide SOC2 artifacts and a small evidence pack for your audit team.

Requested inputs from BlueMesh
- 24h sample traces covering a peak and off-peak window (WAL + token counts + timestamps).
- The 1000-row prompt set you mentioned for quality regression.
- A list of endpoints that must remain under private-only routing.

Attachments included: redwood-topology-diagram.pdf (topology annotated with GPU counts, routing rules, and network flow).

I can produce a one-page cost estimate (TCO) after we receive traces — that will include committed vs burst pricing and an ops runbook for the pilot.

— Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Thanks Jordan / Irene — this is great and matches our notes. A few quick clarifications before we send traces: 
- For the interactive pool you're recommending 8 H100 equiv with floor 4. Can you send a very rough cost delta for committed 4 vs on-demand scaling to 8? Interested in a ballpark monthly run rate for the pilot (approx 600 qps steady).
- For quantization: our QA team will want to see a quality delta report (top-1 / rouge / semantic drift) for int8 vs fp16. Can Redwood run the 1000-row set and return a short quality report?

We're ready to share sample traces tomorrow. Also, Claire and I are available for the SRE workshop on Wed 02/25 afternoon PT — tentative 90 minutes works.

Amit Rangan
